alt: Exercise 3.2 · Q9: In sports events, 19 people wear blue shirts, 15 wear green shirts, 3 wear blue and green, 4 wear a cap and blue shirts, and 2 wear a cap and green shirts, nobody wears all the three items. The total number of people with either a blue or green shirt or cap is 34. How many people are wearing caps?

steps.title: Solution
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\text{Let }B=\text{ blue shirts, }G=\text{ green shirts,}\\[5pt]&\quad C=\text{ caps}\\[5pt]&\text{n(B) }=19,\text{ n(G) }=15,\text{ n(B }\cap \text{ G) }=3,\\[5pt]&\quad \text{n(C }\cap \text{ B) }=4,\text{ n(C }\cap \text{ G) }=2\\[5pt]&\text{n(B }\cap G\cap \text{ C) }=0\\[5pt]&\quad \text{(nobody wears all three items)}\\[5pt]&\text{n(B }\cup G\cup \text{ C) }=34\\[5pt]&\text{n(B }\cup G\cup \text{ C) }=\text{ n(B) }+\text{ n(G) }+\text{ n(C) }-\\[5pt]&\quad \text{n(B }\cap \text{ G) }-\text{ n(C }\cap \text{ B) }-\text{ n(C }\cap \text{ G) }+\\[5pt]&\quad \text{n(B }\cap G\cap \text{ C)}\\[5pt]&34=19+15+\text{ n(C) }-3-4-2+0\\[5pt]&34=34+\text{ n(C) }-9\\[5pt]&\text{n(C) }=9\\[5pt]&\therefore \text{ }\textcolor{#047857}{\mathbf{9}}\text{ people are wearing caps.}\end{aligned}\]
